title: Risk and Prioritization Workflows
summary: Describes repeatable triage flows that convert analytics signals into assignment and remediation actions.

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Prioritization should combine risk signal and delivery capacity. Focusing only on finding volume can stall active remediation when workload and assignment constraints are ignored.

sections.title: Prioritization objective
paragraphs: The goal of dashboard-driven prioritization is to reduce open risk while maintaining sustainable test throughput. Effective prioritization balances severity, exposure concentration, and execution ownership.
RAPTOR provides enough context to move from strategic view to actionable queues without leaving management workflow.

sections.title: Weekly triage sequence
paragraphs: Use a fixed cadence for triage so trend interpretation remains consistent and operational drift is identified early. A weekly cycle generally provides enough signal while staying lightweight.
orderedList: Review `Open Risk Assets` and unresolved indicator movement versus previous period.
Inspect `Top Risk Assets` to validate current high-priority targets.
Check `Tester Workload` for concentration or assignment bottlenecks.
Verify throughput trends to ensure completion keeps pace with starts.
Create filtered Security queues for immediate reassignment or follow-up.

sections.title: Risk tiering approach
paragraphs: A practical risk tiering model is to treat unresolved vulnerable assets with high finding volume as first-tier attention, then address high in-progress concentration to protect cycle time.
Records with completed testing but unresolved risk should remain visible in active management queues until remediation signal is updated.

rows: Open-risk assets with highest finding counts.
Immediate owner alignment and remediation tracking.
In-progress assets with growing vulnerability indicators.
Assignment planning and scheduled start dates.

sections.title: Capacity balancing with workload data
paragraphs: Tester workload panel is intended for assignment balancing decisions. High open-risk concentration under one assignee is a strong signal to consider controlled reassignment where policy permits.
Balance decisions should preserve continuity for complex cases while preventing prolonged queue stagnation.

tip.title: TIP
paragraphs: When reassigning active work, transfer context in notes and ticket links before ownership change so receiving tester can continue without discovery delay.

sections.title: Escalation triggers
paragraphs: Define local escalation thresholds so management response is predictable. Suggested triggers include sustained growth in open-risk assets, falling completion trend, or repeated unassigned backlog in critical apps.
Escalation should result in explicit ownership changes, schedule adjustments, or targeted scope reduction, not only additional reporting.
